summary: Configured persistent resilient static routing between node2 and node3. The direct primary-transit path is preferred, VyOS node1 provides source-preserving fallback, measured failover was 2.008 seconds, and direct-path recovery was 1.004 seconds. All three nodes passed sequential restart persistence testing.
actions_performed: Configured primary-transit as 10.10.0.0/30 and fallback LANs as 10.20.0.0/30 and 10.30.0.0/30.
Installed metric-10 direct and metric-100 fallback static routes with a one-second direct-peer health monitor.
Configured persistent VyOS routes and endpoint-only forwarding with default-drop and no NAT.
Kept management on the separate 10.100.92.0/24 interfaces and outside endpoint routing.
Tested direct failure, fallback convergence, direct-path restoration, and bidirectional source preservation.
Restarted node1, node2, and node3 individually and verified changed boot IDs and recovered state.

evidence.summary: Both endpoints selected metric-10 enp8s0 routes and passed bidirectional source-pinned traffic directly with TTL 64.
After lowering node2 enp8s0, traffic recovered through the metric-100 fallback in 2.008 seconds. TTL 63 and VyOS counters proved forwarding through node1 in both directions.

evidence.requirement: Prefer direct path again after recovery
evidence.summary: The metric-10 direct route returned in 1.004 seconds, followed by symmetric direct routing on both endpoints.

evidence.requirement: Preserve endpoint source addresses and isolate management
evidence.summary: Routes explicitly use 172.20.2.2 and 172.20.3.3 as sources; VyOS forwarded those unchanged. Management remains on enp1s0/eth0 and is absent from endpoint route selection.
Captured healthy baseline and reboot acknowledgement, proved boot ID changed, then verified active VyOS service, restored routes/firewall, and endpoint reachability.
Captured healthy baseline and acknowledgement, proved boot ID changed, and verified persistent addressing, active route monitor, both routes, and bidirectional traffic.
Captured healthy baseline and acknowledgement, proved boot ID changed, and verified persistent addressing, active route monitor, both routes, and endpoint traffic.
Final snapshots show all services active, post-restart boot identities, persistent data-plane state, preferred direct routing, available fallback routes, and successful bidirectional traffic.
